candidate.title: mNET-seq
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina poster row labeled mNET-seq, expanded in the image as native elongating transcript sequencing technology for mammalian chromatin. It depicts native Pol II/chromatin-associated RNA undergoing MNase digestion, recovery as soluble chromatin, Pol II antibody capture, RNA 5′ phosphorylation, purification/size selection, and conversion to cDNA. The leftmost capped elongation icon introduces the assay; it is not an additional processing branch. Neighboring 3′NT method, NET-Seq and PARE-Seq rows are independently labeled context, not grouped targets or interchangeable alternatives. The verified collection page heading and its mNET-seq schematic match this row. Primary Nojima 2015 and 2016 evidence resolves fragment ends, attachment, size-selection meaning and readout for this implementation without adding their unshown experiments, adaptations or detailed library operations.

states.label: Pol II Transcriptome complex
features: Starting material is native mammalian chromatin containing elongating Pol II and its associated nascent RNA; preparation of this fraction is the input boundary, not a separately drawn operation.
The drawing shows purple RNA with an m7G cap at its exposed 5′ end, attached to a blue Pol II complex on chromatin. The cap is descriptive starting context; no cap-selection step is depicted.
For the nascent-transcript component, the terminal synthesized nucleotide has a 3′OH protected within the Pol II active site.

evidence.quote: The hydroxylated 3′ end (3′OH) of the nascent RNA corresponds to the terminal nucleotide synthesized by Pol II (Figure 1A, asterisk). The 5′ end of the cleaved Pol II-associated RNA is also hydroxylated after MNase digestion. To achieve strand-specific RNA sequencing, we carried out a kinase reaction on the IP beads to phosphorylate all nascent RNA 5′ ends but leave the Pol II-embedded 3′OH intact (Figure S1A).

states.label: Soluble chromatin containing Pol II-protected RNA fragments
features: MNase-treated soluble fraction contains released Pol II–RNA complexes; associated RNA is shortened by digestion of exposed nucleic acid.

The drawing also shows detached short blue chromatin fragments and a detached cap-bearing purple RNA fragment. These are digestion products, not a second library route; the onward immunoprecipitation retains Pol II-associated material.

The exposed OH on the retained RNA is interpreted as the MNase-generated 5′OH, consistent with the downstream 5′ phosphorylation caption and the primary papers. The nascent RNA 3′OH remains protected in Pol II.
RNA protected by associated protein complexes, including spliceosomes, can survive alongside active-site nascent RNA.

states.label: Purified, size-selected Pol II-IP RNA
features: RNA is recovered from the captured complexes, separated from DNA and proteins, and selected by size; it is no longer represented as attached to Pol II or beads.
The primary implementation resolves the schematic size-selection step as 35–100-nt RNA. This is a fragment selection, not recovery of full-length capped transcripts.

Selected fragments retain RNA sequence, strand and 3′-end boundaries of the captured nascent or processing-derived molecules. Fragments outside the selected range are not represented by this interface.

evidence.locator: Limitations of mNET-seq, block b00015
evidence.quote: In mNET-seq, 35- to 100-nt RNA fragments are selected and sequenced. Consequently, nascent RNAs shorter than 35 nt (i.e., those within 35 bp of the TSS) cannot be profiled.

states.label: cDNA representing selected Pol II-associated RNA fragments
features: The depicted endpoint is cDNA, the DNA carrier of the selected RNA fragment sequences; sequencing itself is not drawn as a separate operation.
In the primary implementation, directional adapters on the purified RNA support library construction and a sequencing read beginning at the RNA insert 3′ end.
The mapped RNA 3′ nucleotide can report the last base synthesized by engaged Pol II or the position of a co-transcriptional RNA cleavage intermediate. A peak alone need not distinguish these origins.
The library represents the antibody-enriched, nuclease-protected and size-selected population. It does not establish complete recovery of all Pol II-associated RNAs.

operations.label: MNase digestion
operations.description: MNase acts on the starting chromatin complex, digesting accessible DNA and RNA and releasing Pol II-associated, protein-protected RNA fragments into the depicted soluble chromatin fraction. The detached cap-bearing RNA and shortened DNA lines illustrate removed exposed regions; the Pol II-associated fragment follows the onward route.
operations.mechanism: Micrococcal nuclease cleavage of exposed nucleic acid solubilizes chromatin-associated complexes while protected RNA segments survive. The diagram compresses digestion and recovery of the soluble material into this interface.
operations.information_effect: Preserves protected RNA 3′ ends and their association with Pol II-containing complexes while truncating exposed sequence, including the capped upstream region illustrated in the drawing. Nuclease protection is not specific to the Pol II active site; associated protein-protected processing RNA can also survive.

operations.label: 5′ phosphorylation with PNK
operations.description: PNK converts the exposed MNase-generated RNA 5′OH to 5′ phosphate on the immunoprecipitated complexes. operations.mechanism: T4 polynucleotide kinase phosphorylates accessible RNA 5′ hydroxyl ends while the RNA remains on IP beads.
operations.information_effect: Creates the RNA end chemistry needed for later 5′ linker ligation while preserving the original 3′ boundary used for positional readout. This RNA-end modification neither extends the transcript nor changes which Pol II CTD state was captured.

operations.label: Purify and size select
operations.description: Recover RNA from the PNK-treated captured complexes and isolate the selected RNA size fraction. The primary implementation identifies removal of DNA and protein and gel selection of 35–100-nt RNA; the diagram keeps these actions in one broad block.
operations.mechanism: RNA purification followed by size fractionation, releasing RNA from the protein/support association and retaining the selected fragment range.
operations.information_effect: Transfers the selected RNA sequence and 3′-end information into a free-RNA library substrate, while losing the physical complex attachment. Antibody specificity is retained as the preparation provenance. The cited 35–100-nt selection excludes shorter nascent RNAs and limits very promoter-proximal coverage.

operations.label: Reverse transcription
operations.description: The selected RNA is copied into the cDNA endpoint. This is a compressed library-generation interface: the primary method places directional RNA-adapter ligation after purification and before cDNA library construction, but the assigned row does not enumerate those internal library steps.
operations.mechanism: RNA-templated DNA synthesis produces cDNA carrying the selected fragment sequence; the primary-source adapter interface preserves strand and RNA-end orientation.
operations.information_effect: The DNA library carries RNA-fragment sequence and original 3′-end position into downstream sequencing. In the cited method a reverse sequencing primer reads the RNA insert 3′ end, enabling single-nucleotide localization of the Pol II synthesis position or protected processing cleavage end. These origins can produce overlapping types of signal and are not unambiguously distinguished by an individual peak.

method_scopes.rationale: All five operation instances belong to the single continuous mNET-seq route. Soluble chromatin is the state produced by MNase treatment, not a second assay or an extra reagent. The input is the native mammalian chromatin/Pol II complex described by the primary implementation. This scope includes a generic Pol II antibody capture that can target particular CTD states; it does not assert identical complete workflows for other NET-seq methods or instantiate separate antibody branches not drawn here. The OH→P annotation is consistent with 5′ end phosphorylation; primary evidence explicitly distinguishes that exposed end from the preserved Pol II-embedded 3′OH.

checks.rationale: Independent inspection supports the complete candidate at the assigned schematic scope. The single mNET-seq route is represented by six material states, five local operations, and ten matching input/output flows. The leftmost capped elongation icon introduces the method and has no transfer arrow into a second branch. All depicted transformations and the detached digestion products are accounted for; the latter are not retained library branches. Antibody/support attachment persists through PNK and is lost during purification, RNA becomes cDNA only at reverse transcription, and the exposed 5′OH→5′P change is distinguished from the protected nascent 3′OH and from Pol II CTD phosphorylation. Each operation has one material input and one material output; no independent processing is collapsed into a joint operation. Primary evidence supports the implementation and readout limitations; background reviews are explicitly abstract-only and unassigned. No consequential unsupported assertion, omitted target, conflicting interface, or required unresolved correction was found.
